column1: # The original's load-time fix-ups (opence_census::fixups) and how the importer compares: same, differs, replaced or none.

column3: Resolves each call's function by name, as the importer does (Call.function is the name); but it parses string, variable and named constants again from their source text, and fails a script whose non-string constant's written type is not its type ("you need to recompile"). The importer decodes each constant as its written type and keeps a named one's name and index as written; the runtime casts.

A scenario with too many globals or scripts, or a global of no type, has its scripts disabled and still loads; the importer refuses the whole level (the blocks' maxima, value_type's fault). It also grows the string constants by 0x400 for the console, which the engine has no need of. Then hs_compile_postprocess (its own row).

Sets each object name's runtime type and datum from the placements by name index, in object-type order, so the last placement of a name wins. The campaign crate (Mission::new) finds the first placement whose name string matches: a name two placements share resolves to the first, and two names of one string to the same placement.

Sets the linear flag of an interface bitmaps group's images, zeroes a sprite group's sequences' first bitmap index and bitmap count, and drops a last sequence with no bitmaps and no sprites. The importer keeps the flags, counts and sequences as written: the engine's particles, weather and contrails take a sprite group's sequence with no sprites by its bitmap count (the original's zero), and weather counts the dropped sequence. The texture cache's upload (bitmap_verify, texture_cache_bitmap_new) is replaced by the importer's own decoding.
